scope: Independent read-only review of the corrected RecognitionAwareAudioOutput plus LocalSTT and main wiring. No tests, models, services, evaluated-source or test edits during this review.
verdict: No concrete blocking correctness regression found within the wired per-room local recognizer/session scope.

observations.topic: Resume is intercepted before downstream wakeup
observations.assessment: A hold requires the same public current handle captured by pause, pending room recognition, interruptibility and downstream pause capability. A repeated SDK resume remains blocked by the existing hold; an unowned resume directly delegates, including when user_speaking is true. This fixes the independently preserved red case.

The wrapper uses public AudioOutput next_in_chain, base capture/flush bookkeeping and inherited playback event forwarding. It forwards clear_buffer and delegates lifecycle. No installed SDK mutation or private SDK member is used by production changes. Existing component evidence includes real SDK segment/event forwarding; separate generation evidence substitutes only the device AudioSource.

Positive text, failure, cancellation and deadline target only the captured current interruptible handle and keep the sink held until done. Later empty notifications cannot release a cancelling hold. The SDK generation component confirms clear/cleanup and subsequent speech progress for nonempty, error and timeout with its disclosed fake device boundary.

Empty completion requires pending count zero, no newer SDK pause, and user listening to release an owned hold. A new SDK pause invalidates the previous resume request. Loss of interruptibility drops the owned hold without force-interrupting the protected handle.

observations.topic: Late completion after old handle finished
observations.assessment: recognition_completed never acquires a hold. Done/current-handle mismatch clears an old hold; delayed old done/deadline callbacks check captured identity before acting. A new handle cannot inherit the old paused_handle predicate on a normal resume. It can acquire a separate hold only after its own SDK pause and a resume while the room count is still pending; this is the declared room-wide unresolved-recognition policy, not a direct late-callback mutation.

The per-instance counter covers the engine await and SpeechEvent construction, decrements before synchronous completion notification in finally, and distinguishes returned/failed/cancelled. Warmup/direct/whole-span transcription do not enter it. Await cancellation is explicitly not native-inference completion; the saved STT tests verify that distinction.

The public wrapper is installed after session.start and before readiness, only when the selected output can pause. User-state changes notify it. Session close and job cleanup close it idempotently, and job cleanup removes the STT completion callback. Hold timers and handle callbacks are removed; closed/detached wrappers ignore late resume/completion releases.

evidence_limits: The 45 focused/lifecycle and 685 full-suite receipts were produced by root and only inspected here; this review does not claim another test execution.

The final SDK generation exercise uses actual generation/scheduling and does not manually mark handles done, but replaces AudioSource with a zero-queued fake; it is not real transport/native buffering evidence.

Public agent_false_interruption.resumed and agent_state=speaking describe SDK decisions. A suppressed downstream resume can leave those states showing speaking; PCM and recognition_pause telemetry must remain separate in the live audit.

Recognition ownership is per room, not keyed to a transcript/utterance ID. A newly SDK-paused handle may be held while an older room recognition is still pending; this should not be represented as per-request causal attribution.

The hold begins at an SDK resume decision while recognition is already pending. This cannot undo earlier native/device buffering or prevent a resume that occurred before the recognizer await became pending.

Whole output replacement detaches and closes the wrapper. Runtime replace_audio_tail/handoff and arbitrary concurrent custom output mutation are not demonstrated by the current wired session or saved tests.
No live RTC quality, physical audible-stop latency, or general disfluency/noise recovery claim is established by this review.
